claims.text: The proposed material is a WMoTaNb refractory high-entropy alloy containing 5–10 vol% Cu.
A post-sintering treatment at approximately 700°C for 15–30 minutes in an inert atmosphere will produce uniformly dispersed, coherent Cu nanoprecipitates in the WMoTaNb matrix.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates can be produced in a tungsten-based refractory HEA through controlled thermomechanical processing.
In situ TEM or synchrotron XRD monitoring can ensure uniform Cu nanoprecipitate nucleation, growth, and maintained coherence during the proposed treatment.
Copper has intrinsically high thermal conductivity.
Uniformly dispersed Cu nanoprecipitates will form continuous high-thermal-conductivity pathways through the HEA.
The Cu nanoprecipitate pathways will enhance both electron-mediated and phonon-mediated heat transfer.
Coherent Cu–HEA interfaces will minimize interfacial stress concentrations.
The coherent Cu nanoprecipitates will support dislocation-bypass mechanisms that preserve mechanical integrity.
Coherent nanoprecipitate architectures in a tungsten-based refractory HEA can coexist with yield strength above 2 GPa and approximately 15% uniform tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
A coherent-nanoprecipitate tungsten-based refractory HEA can retain a yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800°C.
The proposed treatment will increase effective thermal conductivity by approximately 20–30% relative to the as-sintered alloy.
The treated WMoTaNb–Cu alloy will retain high yield strength and ductility at approximately 800°C under dynamic loading.
Plasma-facing reactor components expose materials to high temperatures and high heat fluxes.
The proposed performance should hold under sustained thermal flux producing local temperatures up to approximately 800°C and under reactor-representative dynamic mechanical loading.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of interface coherence may diminish the thermal-conductivity enhancement.
Precipitate coarsening or incoherent interfaces may degrade mechanical properties.
The experiment compares heat-treated and untreated Cu-doped WMoTaNb specimens under the same simulated thermal and mechanical conditions.
Thermal conductivity, yield strength, ductility, and precipitate morphology and coherence will be measured.
The hypothesis is declared falsified by less than a 10% conductivity improvement or by a greater than 10% reduction in yield strength or ductility relative to the untreated control.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 20–30% conductivity increase, but the falsification rule only rejects increases below 10%. An observed increase of 10–19% would contradict the quantified prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.

The intervention defines the treatment as 700°C in an inert atmosphere, while the conditions field says the treatment itself is conducted under simulated reactor thermal flux reaching about 800°C and dynamic loading. It is unclear whether reactor simulation applies only to subsequent testing or also to the heat treatment.
